## 23 Sept 2026: Phase 146j

### `src/modules/claims/document-reading.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE DOCUMENT READER'S TWO FOLLOW-ONS.   Phase 146i, 23 September 2026.
  >
  > Phase 146g wired the reader into the upload flow and left it switched off. Two things about it were true from
  > that day and neither had anywhere to live. They are here together because they are one story: what a reading can
  > keep, and what a person is told about a reading that did not work.
  >
  > ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  > 1 · THE TWO FIELDS NOBODY CAN VOUCH FOR
  >
  > `assertClaimsWritable` (09-app/backend/src/modules/claims/documents/client-doc-ingestion.ts) keeps two CLIENT_DOC fields only
  > on the footing that their value names an ORGANISATION: `grant_funder_name` ("the funding body, not an
  > individual") and `brc_issuing_body` (a local authority rather than an individual approved inspector). The name
  > exclusion register classifies by field NAME and never sees a value, so it cannot tell one from the other; the
  > caller must assert it, and an absent assertion fails closed. That refusal is CORRECT AND IS NOT TOUCHED HERE.
  >
  > WHAT WAS WRONG IS THAT NOBODY COULD EVER ANSWER IT. `UploadReading.discriminants` defaulted to `{}`, so a grant
  > funding agreement and a building regulations completion certificate had EVERY one of their claims refused — not
  > merely the one field — and the upload reported that nothing was kept. A document type that can never be
  > captured is not a control, it is a hole with a lock on it.
  >
  > SO THE ANSWER IS A PERSON'S, AND IT IS RECORDED. It cannot be inferred from the document; inferring it is
  > exactly what the control exists to prevent. It is asked on the document's own page, of Admin or Sales, and kept
  > against the LOGICAL document rather than one upload of it: a second version of the same agreement is the same
  > agreement, and the answer stands until somebody changes it.
  >
  > AND "NOT SURE" IS "NOT ANSWERED". Only `yes` lets the field be kept. `no`, `not_sure` and no row at all are the
  > same decision, and none of them becomes a guess, a blank or a pass — N4. The row exists so that "somebody looked
  > and was not sure" can be told from "nobody has been asked", which is a fact about the work and not about the
  > claim.
  >
  > ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  > 2 · WHAT HAPPENED WHEN WE READ IT
  >
  > `finishUpload` has returned a `ReadingOutcome` with a reason in plain words since Phase 146g, and nothing drew
  > it anywhere: a document that was sent and came back unreadable looked exactly like one nobody had asked about.
  > One row per reading, and the staff document page draws it.
  >
  > A READING THAT NEVER STARTED IS NOT A READING. No row is written where no reader was wired in, or where
  > `CLAUDE_SWITCHES.DOCUMENT_READING` is false — which is how this ships. With the switch off a finished upload
  > must behave exactly as it did before Phase 146g, and a row is a difference.
  >
  > NEVER A WORD OF THE DOCUMENT, on the screen or in the row. What is kept is a state, a count and a reason.
  >
  > ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  > 3 · PHASE 146j, 25 September 2026 — THE TWO ONE-WAY DOORS 146i LEFT, CLOSED THE WAY A PICK IS TAKEN BACK
  >
  > (a) A YES CAN BE TAKEN BACK. A 'yes' lets the next reading keep the name, through `ingestRegisterRecord`, as part
  >     of that version's CLIENT_DOC record. Changing the answer to 'no' afterwards changed nothing already written.
  >     Now a 'yes' that has kept something is taken back by its own act, which asks why (`withdrawVouch` in
  >     src/modules/claims/documents.ts): it takes THAT FIELD, AND NO OTHER, out of every record it went into, and leaves the
  >     answer on its row with who withdrew it, when and why. A withdrawn yes keeps nothing, exactly as a 'no' does, and
  >     the row still says it was a yes. The plain buttons will not turn a yes that kept something into a 'no'.
  >
  > (b) THE QUESTION IS ASKED BEFORE THE FIRST READING. The document's page exists only once the file has been read
  >     and deleted, so the first reading of a grant funding agreement always left the funder's name out. The staff
  >     upload forms and the document request now ask it where the type is chosen. IT IS STILL ONE STORE: the upload
  >     writes the same row against the document it creates, and a request writes it against itself, to be ADOPTED —
  >     the same row, its document filled in — by the document that answers the request, before that document is
  >     read. The page's answer governs: where the document already has one, an earlier answer is not adopted and
  >     does not replace it, and whatever is on the page afterwards is what the next reading reads.

  > turns ONE source on for ONE call, in a map of its own, in a command a person typed.

### `src/core/custom-roles.ts`

- Line 1:

  > ROLES A SUPER ADMIN CAN MAKE. Phase 151, 24 September 2026.
  >
  > WHAT LAKHBIR DECIDED (Word answers 39 and 40, closed 24 September 2026). The super admin must be able to create
  > roles, choose what each can see and do, and give people roles.
  >
  > HOW A ROLE IS MADE, AND WHY THIS SHAPE. A role the super admin makes is a NAME and a LIST OF GRANTS. Each grant is one
  > action the back office knows (src/core/authz.ts, REGISTERED_ACTIONS) together with THE BUILT-IN ROLE WHOSE RULE IT BORROWS
  > — "claim.read, as Sales reads it". So a made role never invents a rule: every yes it can give is a yes one of the four
  > staff roles already gives, with that role's test on the specific object (the assigned surveyor's own job, the owner's
  > own task, the organisation's own documents). Authorisation stays on the server, for each request and each object,
  > exactly as it is for the built-in roles: `can()` in src/core/authz.ts decides a made role by the same table.
  >
  > THE HARD LIMITS. No role editor may break these, and a role that would is REFUSED WITH A PLAIN SENTENCE
  > (`roleRefusal`), never saved in part:
  >   1. THE SURVEYOR NEVER RECEIVES THE ESTIMATE. A role that can survey — any grant borrowed from Surveying, or the
  >      right to sign a survey off — may hold none of the actions that reveal the estimate or the value of a claim
  >      (SEALED_FROM_SURVEY). And a made role is sent to the estimate quarantine AS THE SURVEYOR unless it holds
  >      `estimate.read` itself (src/core/roles.ts, toQuarantineRole), so the survey workspace's payload withholds the sealed
  >      estimate from it; test/phase151.test.ts runs payload-proof's check on such a role.
  >   2. ONLY THE SUPER ADMIN RUNS ACCOUNTS AND ROLES. Creating, changing and disabling users, giving roles, and making
  >      or changing roles (NEVER_GRANTED) cannot be given to a made role.
  >   3. A GRANT MUST BE ONE THE BUILT-IN ROLE ACTUALLY HOLDS. A client's rule is never borrowed: a made role is a staff
  >      role, and the client's own-organisation rule would give a staff member a client's view.
  >   4. EVERY CHANGE IS IN THE AUDIT LOG — made, changed, refused and given (src/web/role-editor.ts).
  >
  > WHERE THEY LIVE. The `custom_roles` and `custom_role_grants` tables (migration 046), and a row in `roles`, so a user
  > holding one is held by the database's own reference. This module keeps the set in memory for `can()`, which is pure;
  > `loadCustomRoles` fills it when the application starts and after every change.
  >
  > THIS FILE IMPORTS NOTHING FROM src/core/authz.ts, on purpose: authz.ts reads it, and the validation is handed the one fact
  > it needs about the built-in table (`holds`) by its caller.

## 24 Sept 2026: Phase 151c

### `src/integrations/connectors/ostn15.ts`

- Line 1:

  > LATITUDE AND LONGITUDE TO BRITISH NATIONAL GRID, EXACTLY — OR NOT AT ALL. Phase 151a, 24 September 2026.
  >
  > The land boundary files are in British National Grid (EPSG:27700), metres. A point given as latitude and longitude
  > must be converted before it can be looked for, and HM Land Registry warns that a rough conversion can move features
  > by up to 15 metres (04-phase-work/phase133/inspire-format-findings.md) — enough to put a property in the wrong
  > parcel. Ordnance Survey's own guide says a Helmert-type conversion is good to "only about 3 metres". So this file
  > does ONE conversion, the one Ordnance Survey defines as exact for this purpose, OSTN15, and refuses otherwise.
  >
  > OSTN15, AS ORDNANCE SURVEY PUBLISHES IT ("A guide to coordinate systems in Great Britain", docs.os.uk, read
  > 24 September 2026, and the OSTN15 developer pack):
  >   1. the ETRS89 latitude and longitude are projected with the National Grid's Transverse Mercator projection on
  >      the GRS80 ellipsoid (true origin 49°N 2°W, scale 0.9996012717, false origin 400 km west and 100 km north);
  >   2. "the grids of northing and easting shifts between ETRS89 and OSGB36 cover Britain at a resolution of one
  >      kilometre": the four grid points around the projected point give its shift "by a bilinear interpolation";
  >   3. the shift is added. The result is the OSGB36 National Grid easting and northing — EPSG:27700.
  >
  > WHAT IS REFUSED, AND WHY EACH IS A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A ROUGHER ANSWER:
  >   · no grid file on this server — the shifts ARE the conversion; without them there is only an approximation;
  >   · a datum that is not stated as ETRS89. OSTN15 converts ETRS89. WGS84 drifts away from ETRS89 by about 2.5 cm a
  >     year (around a metre by 2026), and a supplier that does not say which it gives is not assumed to give either;
  >   · a point outside the grid, or where any of the four surrounding grid points is missing or marked outside the
  >     transformation's area (datum flag 0) — the interpolation would then be from shifts OSTN15 does not vouch for.
  >
  > THE GRID FILE is Ordnance Survey's OSTN15_OSGM15_DataFile.txt from the free developer pack (BSD licence), kept on
  > this server OUTSIDE the repository and named by CAPREBATE_OSTN15_FILE — like the ONS postcode table, a deployment
  > artefact, absent by default. ABSENT, every latitude and longitude is refused and nothing else changes. The first
  > copy put on a server must be checked against the pack's own test points (tools/ostn15-verify.ts) before it is
  > trusted. No file was downloaded by the phase that built this. Phase 151a's addendum (24 September 2026) put OS's full
  > developer pack on the Mac, in ~/caprebate-data/ostn15/, outside the repository, and the check passed on all forty
  > test points. Phase 151c: the demo launcher names that file when it is there (tools/demo-server.cjs).

  > when a signature holds - X-Signature-V2 (the HMAC of the sorted, compact JSON, Didit's recommended one) or
  > X-Signature (the HMAC of the exact bytes) - AND its X-Timestamp is within five minutes. Only these map to an answer:
  > Approved -> PASS; Declined -> FAIL; In Review, Resubmitted and Kyc Expired -> REFER; Expired and Abandoned ->
  > NOT_COMPLETED. Not Started, In Progress and Awaiting User are the check still under way: acknowledged, and NOT kept as
  > a result. ANY OTHER STATUS, A MISSING ONE, OR A BAD SIGNATURE IS NEVER A PASS: an unknown status is REFER, for a person
  > to look at, and an unsigned or stale body is refused outright. A webhook about anything but a session's status is
  > acknowledged and ignored.
  >
  > WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It never finishes a check on its own. A PASS is recorded on the check as evidence of how
  > identity was verified; a person still completes the check (`completeCheck` in src/web/compliance-aml.ts), as today.
  > And we keep our own record of the decision, whatever retention is set in Didit's console: the money-laundering
  > rules ask us to keep our evidence for five years.

  > not money-laundering supervision applies (Word question 10, recorded 24 September 2026, Lakhbir in chat: "we still
  > check for identity"), so NOTHING HERE READS AML_IN_SCOPE: a check can be sent for any client, from the client's own
  > record or from an open customer due diligence check.
  >
  > THE CONNECTOR IS src/integrations/connectors/identity-check.ts (Phase 151), and it decides whether anything leaves this server:
  > `startIdentityCheck` refuses before any call while `identityCheckMissing` lists anything — the service named in the
  > privacy notice and in clause 7 of the engagement letter, its three entries in the key file, and the IDENTITY_CHECK switch,
  > which ships false. OFF, A PERSON WHO PRESSES "SEND" IS TOLD, IN WORDS, WHAT IS STILL MISSING, AND NOTHING IS SENT.
  > This file adds no second switch and no second gate.
  >
  >   sendIdentityCheck      compliance.write only (Admin today). The contact being checked must be a contact of the
  >                          organisation; a due diligence check it is sent from must be that organisation's and open.
  >                          The first and last name go to the service in the call and nowhere else — not in a row, not
  >                          in the audit log. What is kept is migration 047's identity_checks row: whose check, from
  >                          where, the service's session id and the link the client follows, who sent it and when.
  >   receiveIdentityResult  the route the service calls, POST /hooks/identity-check, with no login (the service has
  >                          none; the address is set in Didit's console). The body is believed only when a signature
  >                          holds and it is under five minutes old (`readIdentityDecision`): A BAD OR MISSING SIGNATURE,
  >                          OR A STALE ONE, IS REFUSED, AUDITED AS IDENTITY_RESULT_REFUSED, AND NOTHING IS WRITTEN. A
  >                          signed word that the check is still under way, or about something other than a check's
  >                          status, is acknowledged and not kept (IDENTITY_RESULT_NOT_KEPT): it is not a result.
  >                          So is a signed result for a session we never sent. A result that holds is kept as OUR OWN
  >                          COPY (identity_check_results, append-only: the decision's fields, the SHA-256 of the exact
  >                          body, never a name, a document number or an image — `identityResultCopy`), because the
  >                          service keeps its copy for a short time only and the money-laundering rules ask a firm to
  >                          keep its evidence for five years.
  >   A PASS IS EVIDENCE OF HOW IDENTITY WAS VERIFIED. When the latest result on a check sent from an OPEN due diligence
  >                          check is PASS and that check's "How it was verified" is still empty, it is filled in with a
  >                          dated sentence naming the service, and CDD_CHECK_UPDATED says so. A person still finishes
  >                          the check (`completeCheck`), as before; a PASS never finishes anything on its own.
  >
  > N4. An unknown status is REFER, never PASS (the connector). A check with no result yet reads "no result yet" — never
  > as a pass and never as a failure.

### `src/integrations/connectors/signatory-check.ts`

- Line 1:

  > WHO SIGNED, AND WHETHER THE PUBLIC REGISTER SAYS THEY MAY SIGN — CHECKED IN MEMORY, KEPT AS YES OR NO.
  > Phase 151b, 25 September 2026. Switched off WITH THE LOOKUPS: no switch of its own.
  >
  > ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  > THE DECISION
  >
  > Word question 156, for the data protection officer: "May we briefly check two public register names without saving
  > them?" The background: we want to know that the person who signed the engagement letter really represents the
  > business, and two free public sources can say — the Companies House officers list, and the care regulator's (CQC's)
  > named people, the registered manager and the nominated individual. The suggestion was to read only the names,
  > compare them in memory and throw them away, keeping a yes or no and the source; never to store an officer's name;
  > to record "not found" as just that, never as a risk; and never to show it to the client.
  >
  > ANSWER, closed 24 September 2026: "Yes – best to check who signs and if they have authority". The action plan:
  > "check who signs and whether they have authority against the public register, reading names in memory and keeping
  > only yes or no; switched off with the lookups."
  >
  > ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  > WHAT IT DOES
  >
  > `checkSignatory` takes the name the signer typed on the engagement letter (engagement_signatures.signer_name,
  > migration 040 — read by src/web/research.ts on the server, never from a form), the client's company number and care
  > regulator ids that we already hold, and the client's claimant type. For each of the two registers it gives:
  >
  >   YES          the register names them in a role that can sign: a CURRENT director (or an LLP's designated
  >                member) at Companies House; the registered manager or the nominated individual at CQC.
  >   NO           the register answered and does not name them so: not listed, listed only as having left, or
  >                listed in a role that cannot sign (a secretary, an ordinary LLP member). NOT A RISK AND NOT A
  >                WARNING: it is what the register shows, and the words say so and nothing more.
  >   NOT_CHECKED  with a reason code: switched off, free lookups not open, the letter not signed, no key, no name, no
  >                company number or care registration, a sole trader or partnership (the register does not apply),
  >                the register did not answer, could not be read, or listed too many people to read.
  >
  > NAMES NEVER LEAVE: the signer's name is held in the closure of `signerTest` and nowhere else; the register's names
  > are read inside the connectors (src/integrations/connectors/companies-house.ts `companiesHouseOfficers`, src/integrations/connectors/cqc.ts
  > `cqcNamedPeople`) and dropped there. The outcome carries a source, a result, a reason CODE and the words for it. No
  > name is in the outcome, the stored row (migration 050 has no name column, and its reason is a closed list of codes),
  > the audit row (SIGNATORY_CHECKED: source and result), a log line or an error. Nothing here throws, and nothing
  > here writes: src/web/research.ts stores the outcome.
  >
  > ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  > THE GATES AND THE SWITCHES — THE LOOKUPS' OWN, NOT NEW ONES
  >
  > Both registers are free, so the check waits on the free gate (CB_REGISTRY.precondition, read by research.ts's
  > `freeGate` and passed in here). It also waits on the signed engagement, asserted server-side by
  > `assertSignedEngagement`, because until the letter is signed there is no signer to check. Then the SOURCE'S OWN
  > SWITCH: Companies House's is CH_COMPANY, the care regulator's is CQC (REGISTER_SWITCHES, both false). Then the key.
  > Each is checked through `runConnector`, the same path every lookup takes, so a call is made only after all four.
  >
  > ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  > HOW TWO NAMES ARE COMPARED — `sameName`
  >
  > matching.ts scores addresses and company names; a person's name needs a stricter rule, so it is written here and
  > tested. Both names are put in capitals, accents dropped, full stops and apostrophes removed, and titles (Dr, Mr, Mrs,
  > Prof …) and letters after a name (OBE, Jr, PhD …) dropped. Companies House writes "SURNAME, Forenames"; a name with
  > a comma is read that way round. A name with no comma is tried at every split, so an unhyphenated double surname
  > still matches. A hyphen inside a surname is ignored ("Smith-Jones" = "Smith Jones"). Then:
  >   · the surnames must be the same;
  >   · the FIRST forename must be the same, in full — an initial alone is never enough;
  >   · middle names are optional on either side, but where both give them they must agree, in order, in full or as an
  >     initial ("Joseph A" matches "Joseph Andrew"; "Joseph Brian" does not).
  > Anything short of that is not the same name. A false NO costs a person a look; a false YES would be a check that
  > lied, so the rule leans to NO. Nicknames are not guessed.

  > Caprebate — AI Document Pipeline
  > Board item 12830166311. Phase 3, item 5.
  >
  > Clients upload planning documents, fire risk assessments, O&M manuals,
  > asbestos registers, insurance reinstatement valuations, leases and contractor

  >
  > ============================================================================
  > ABSOLUTE RULE: PLANNING COMMENT TEXT NEVER REACHES A MODEL.
  >
  > Planning portals carry objector and neighbour names and addresses — third
  > party personal data with no lawful basis for us to process. The rule is not
  > negotiable and is not enforced by remembering it.
  >
  > It is enforced structurally, in four layers:
  >
  >   L1  NOT ACQUIRED   the planning fetcher never calls a comments endpoint.
  >                      You cannot leak what you do not hold. (Item 12830181420
  >                      already refuses to store the fields.)
  >   L2  DISCARDED      uploaded planning PDFs are segmented, and every segment
  >                      classified as representations / consultee responses /

  > `libsql` package answers the same way (better-sqlite3's API, synchronous, the same SQL dialect, STRICT tables
  > included), so nothing above this class changes. A Postgres driver answers later (a promise), and would change
  > every one of those calls. The package is loaded only when it is asked for, so memory and file never touch it.

### `src/core/mfa-seal.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE AUTHENTICATOR APP'S SECRET, SEALED AT REST. Phase 151k, 28 September 2026.
  >
  > Phase 151j kept the shared secret of a person's authenticator app as text: `users.mfa_secret`, and while they set it
  > up `sign_in_steps.pending_secret`. Anybody who could read the database could then make that person's codes. So the
  > secret is now SEALED with AES-256-GCM under a key read the way every other key is read (src/core/secrets.ts): the name
  > CAPREBATE_MFA_KEY in the key file outside the repository (never a key file inside it), or on the test website its
  > own settings (api/index.mjs, TEST_DEPLOY_KEYS). The key is 32 bytes, written as base64:
  >     node -e "console.log(require('node:crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"
  >
  > THREE STATES, AND NOTHING SET UP TODAY STOPS WORKING:
  >   NONE   no key set. A new secret is kept as text, exactly as before this phase, and a text one is read.
  >   KEY    a good key. A new secret is sealed. A text one is still read - and sealed the next time it is used to sign
  >          in (src/core/sign-in.ts), or all at once by `node src/core/cli.ts seal-app-secrets`.
  >   BAD    a key is set but is not 32 bytes of base64. Nothing new is written with it, and it opens nothing: it refuses
  >          in words, because keeping a secret as text while somebody believes it is sealed is worse than saying so.
  > A SEALED SECRET WITHOUT ITS KEY IS REFUSED IN WORDS (the key removed, or changed): never read as text, never a crash.
  >
  > WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: `cbmfa1:` then base64 of a 12-byte nonce, the 16-byte tag and the sealed bytes. The person's id
  > is bound in as additional data, so a sealed secret copied onto another person's row does not open. A text secret is
  > base32 and can never start with `cbmfa1:`, so the two forms are told apart without a column saying which.

  > AUTHENTICATOR-APP CODES — RFC 6238 (TOTP) over RFC 4226 (HOTP). Phase 151j, 28 September 2026.
  >
  > The standard every authenticator app speaks (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password and the rest):
  > a shared secret, HMAC-SHA1, a 30-second step, six digits. Written here on node:crypto rather than taken from a
  > package, because it is thirty lines and the RFC's own test vectors (in test/phase151j.test.ts) prove it.
  >
  >   newSecret        20 random bytes, base32 - what the person's app is given, by QR code or typed in
  >   otpauthUri       the address a QR code carries: otpauth://totp/<issuer>:<account>?secret=...&issuer=...
  >   codeAt           the six digits for one time step
  >   verifyCode       a code checked against the step before, the step now and the step after (a phone's clock may
  >                    be up to thirty seconds out), and NEVER a step at or before the last one accepted, so a code
  >                    seen over someone's shoulder cannot be used again. Returns the step it matched, or null.

### `src/core/db.ts`

- Line 313:

  > Migrations, applied in filename order and recorded so they run once.
  >
  > Deliberately dumb: no down-migrations, no checksums-with-auto-repair. A
  > migration that has run is recorded; a new one runs; anything else is a
  > person's decision, not a framework's.
  >
  > PHASE 152 (the sweep, 28 September 2026): A FILE AND ITS RECORD LAND TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL. Until now a file ran,
  > and THEN its schema_migrations row was written, so a start cut off between the two left the file's tables made and
  > unrecorded - and every later start failed on them ("table claim_facts already exists", the test website's first
  > start on Turso, 28 Sep 2026, stopped by a 30-second limit). Now the record is written inside the same transaction as
  > the file's own statements, so a cut-off start leaves either both or neither, and the next start finishes the job.
  > Two shapes, and only two:
  >   - a PLAIN file: it and its record run in one transaction here (Db.tx);
  >   - a file that RUNS ITS OWN TRANSACTION (007, 011, 014, 016 to 019, 049, 053, 054, 056): `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF;`,
  >     a line `BEGIN;`, its body, a line `COMMIT;`, `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;`. The pragma cannot change inside a
  >     transaction and a transaction cannot begin inside another, so it is split at its own BEGIN and COMMIT: the pragma
  >     runs outside, the body AND the record run in one transaction, and the closing pragma always runs after.
  > Anything else - two BEGINs, a COMMIT with no BEGIN, a transaction statement in a plain file, anything but the one
  > pragma around a file's own transaction - is REFUSED with a sentence, never guessed at.

### `src/shared/shared-objectstore.ts`

- Line 1:

  > PHASE 151i, 28 September 2026 — THE DOCUMENT STORE EVERY COPY OF THE TEST WEBSITE REACHES. BUILT AND SWITCHED OFF.
  >
  > Phase 151e gave the test website one lasting database (Turso) for every copy of it. Its uploaded documents still went
  > to a folder on each copy's temporary disk, so a document uploaded through one copy was missing from the next while its
  > row said it was there. This store keeps them in ONE PRIVATE VERCEL BLOB STORE instead. api/index.mjs uses it only when
  > the lasting database is in use AND a Blob store is connected (`sharedDocumentStore` there); anything less keeps the
  > temporary folder, exactly as before.
  >
  > WHAT CHANGES AND WHAT DOES NOT. `SharedObjectStore` IS an `FsObjectStore`: every caller keeps the type it was written
  > against, and every rule stays where it was — the key checked, an original sealed (AES-256-GCM) before it is kept and
  > refused with no key, a deletion proved, a write capability scoped to exactly one key. It replaces only the four
  > steps that say where the bytes go (`readBytes`, `writeBytes`, `copyBytes`, `removeProven`). The port
  > (`ObjectStore` in the upload handler) already answers with promises, so no caller changed to suit a store.
  >
  > PRIVATE, NEVER A PUBLIC ADDRESS. Read from Vercel's docs, 28 Sep 2026 (vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage):
  > a private store's objects "require authentication for all read and write operations"; its address,
  > https://<store>.private.blob.vercel-storage.com/<path>, "is not publicly accessible". And here:
  >   - every call says access: 'private' — a PUBLIC store refuses it, so a store created public by mistake fails closed;
  >   - the address Blob gives back on a write is thrown away, never stored, logged or sent;
  >   - a document leaves only through the routes that already authorise each request (the kept original's download,
  >     the photograph), which read it here server-side. The upload link is still OURS (`/upload/put?token=…`), never
  >     a Blob address, and still scoped to one key;
  >   - every read skips Blob's cache (useCache: false) — the latest bytes, and nothing served from a copy on the way;
  >   - every write says application/octet-stream, so nothing is ever rendered as a page, and the least cache time
  >     Blob allows (60 seconds). Blob's docs: a deleted object "may take up to one minute" to leave its cache. That
  >     cache is behind the same authentication; the Developer Spec's "Built by Phase 151i" section says so plainly.
  >
  > ONE UPLOAD LINK SECRET FOR EVERY COPY. A link issued by one copy is sent back to whichever copy Vercel picks. With a
  > secret made fresh in each process, the second copy refuses a good link. So the shared store signs links with a secret
  > derived (HKDF-SHA256) from the lasting database's token, which every copy already holds and nothing else sees. A new
  > database token ends links issued before it — they last fifteen minutes anyway.
  >
  > THE BLOB CLIENT IS A PORT, LIKE THE STORE. `BlobClient` is the four things this store asks of Blob, in our words.
  > `vercelBlobClient` is the real one: @vercel/blob, loaded only when the store is switched on, so the memory and folder
  > modes never load it. PHASE 161a, 4 Nov 2026 (the ITRoadway audit): the back end lists @vercel/blob for the tests only,
  > so the live install (npm ci --omit=dev) does not contain it; the root package.json, which builds only the test
  > website, keeps it; and api/index.mjs keeps the folder, and says why, if a store is set but the package is missing. The tests hand in a client that answers as Blob's documented SDK does, with no network.

### `src/integrations/connectors/turnstile.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE CONTACT FORM'S SECURITY CHECK, ON THE SERVER — Cloudflare Turnstile. 29 September 2026.
  >
  > The home page (Caprebate/09-app/site/home.html) runs Cloudflare's check in the visitor's browser and posts its answer
  > with the enquiry as `cf-turnstile-response`. A check that runs only in the browser stops nothing: a script posts to
  > /enquiry without ever loading the page. So before an enquiry is kept, this asks Cloudflare whether that answer is
  > real (its "siteverify" call), through src/integrations/connectors/http.ts like every other outside call.
  >
  > THREE STATES, EACH SAID IN WORDS:
  >   · NO SECRET KEY in the key file (TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY): nothing is checked and the enquiry is kept as before. The
  >     start-up log says so, and the enquiry's audit line records "not_checked".
  >   · A KEY, BUT THE TRANSFER IS NOT APPROVED. Cloudflare is a US company, and src/integrations/connectors/sources.ts refuses a call
  >     outside the UK and EU until the data protection officer approves it (`international_transfer_approved`). Until
  >     then nothing is sent, nothing is checked, the enquiry is kept, and the log and the audit line say why. Approving
  >     it is one word in sources.ts, and it is Sadique's decision, not a build one.
  >   · A KEY AND APPROVAL: the answer is checked. No answer, an answer Cloudflare rejects, or no reply from Cloudflare
  >     each REFUSES the enquiry: nothing is kept, the audit says which, and the person is told in plain words.
  >
  > THE SITE KEY (TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY) is public by design — it is printed in the page — and is put into the home page's
  > script when it is served (src/web/home-site.ts). Without one, the page keeps Cloudflare's published TEST key.
  > No key is ever printed: the secret goes only into the call's body, which no record keeps.

  >
  > THE LINK GOES OUT WITH THE INVITATION. The email and its calendar file carry OUR join page (/call/<token>), where
  > the client joins inside our site, and Zoom's own link and passcode for anyone who would rather use the Zoom app.
  > Emails leave when email sending is switched on (EMAIL_SENDING); until then they wait in the outbox, like every other.
  >
  > STAFF JOIN FROM THE BACK OFFICE (/staff/calls/<booking>/video) as the host; the client joins at /call/<token> as a
  > participant, into the waiting room. Both pages run Zoom's Web SDK (component view) from source.zoom.us, under a
  > security policy of their own that allows exactly that and nothing else from outside (VIDEO_PAGE_HEADERS). Our script
  > (/assets/video-call.js) joins only when the person presses "Join", so no camera is asked for on arrival.
  >
  > WITHOUT ZOOM (no keys yet, or the transfer not approved) nothing here makes a meeting; the call still stands, the

  >     invitation (`videoJoinWords`). Gone once ZOOM_PLAN says a paid plan.
  >   · ONE CALL AT A TIME (`videoCallsAtSameTime`, `SAME_TIME_WORDS`): one Zoom user hosts one meeting at a time, so a
  >     video call booked over another with the same host is warned about wherever it is booked or moved. A warning,
  >     never a refusal.
  >   · HOW LONG IT LASTED (`checkCallLength`): a member of staff asks Zoom after the call; two numbers are kept
  >     (migration 091), or the screen says our plan does not give them.

### `src/modules/survey/pack-lines.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE SURVEY PACK'S LINES — from the fixture list, never invented. 1 October 2026.
  >
  > Every line a pack starts with is a row of `02-modules-and-build-prep/Caprebate-Fixture-Taxonomy-v1.csv` (103 rows,
  > each with its statutory authority and its pool), for the building's sector and the rows every sector shares. This
  > file reads that list from the app's own copy (`backend/copies/`, Phase 161d1), kept byte for byte the same as the
  > original by `npm run lint:copies`; nothing here re-types it.
  >
  > WHICH ROWS: those that can go in a pool through a survey — main pool (MP), special rate (SR), and the two the list
  > leaves to the surveyor (APPORTION, and builder's work that FOLLOWS_PLANT, whose pool is the plant's). NOT: loose
  > equipment (MP_AIA — the accountant's claim from the fixed-asset register, not a fixture), anything excluded (NONE),
  > and the structures allowance (SBA — a different relief).
  >
  > WHAT IS DRAFTED, AND ONLY FROM EVIDENCE (src/modules/crm/rooms.ts: "a seeded count would be this system inventing a property
  > fact"):
  >   · the share that qualifies, where the list gives one (a number, with its authority): Cap Rebate's DRAFT;
  >   · the pool, where the list gives one: DRAFT;
  >   · how much, ONLY where the list measures the row against something we hold — the floor area (from the energy
  >     certificate) for a whole-building system, or a room count the surveyor has recorded, for a row counted per room.
  >     Everything else is left for the surveyor.
  >   · the rate: PHASE 159f (Lakhbir, 9 October 2026: "With BCIS data loaded, the pack could draft each rate from the
  >     right building type — this needs to happen"). The whole-building rate and every line measured by floor area are
  >     drafted from BCIS in src/modules/survey/bcis-data.ts (NRM_OF_LINE), at the purchase date; the surveyor accepts or overrides
  >     each, with a source. A line counted per room or per item is not drafted: BCIS prices elements per m² of floor.

### `src/modules/survey/survey-pack.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE SURVEY PACK — the drafts, the surveyor's stamped changes, and the sums. 1 October 2026.
  >
  > Lakhbir: "the idea is API's do most of the work, they check and approve" and "any edits made by the surveyor needs to
  > essentially have their stamp to say thats their number".
  >
  > A VALUE IS ONE OF THREE THINGS, AND THE PACK ALWAYS SAYS WHICH:
  >   EVIDENCE  read from a record we hold: the energy certificate's floor area, the title register's price, the room
  >             counts recorded on the job;
  >   DRAFT     Cap Rebate's, from the fixture list: a line's pool and the share that qualifies, with its authority;
  >   SURVEYOR  typed by the surveyor: their name, the time and their reason, kept for ever (migration 070).
  > Nothing else fills a box. A value we do not hold is NEEDED, and the sums give no total until it is there
  > (src/modules/survey/pack-sums.ts). PHASE 159f: rates are DRAFTED from BCIS (src/modules/survey/bcis-data.ts) — the whole-building rate and every
  > line measured by floor area — at the purchase date; the surveyor accepts each or types their own with its source.
  >
  > WHO MAY CHANGE IT: the surveyor the job is assigned to (`surveyor_job.commit`, the rule the workspace's figures use).
  > Everyone who may open the job may read the pack.
  >
  > TWO TABS NEVER OVERWRITE EACH OTHER UNSEEN. Every page carries the pack's counter as it was drawn; a change sent from
  > an older page is refused and the page is drawn again with what changed. The check and the write are one transaction.
  >
  > THE PRICE IS IN THE PACK. The workspace withholds a register's price from a surveyor (REGISTER_AMOUNTS_WITHHELD, so
  > they cannot anchor on it). The pack cannot: section 562 shares out the price, so the price is its first input. This
  > follows Lakhbir's decision of 1 October 2026 that the surveyor works from a pre-filled pack and approves it.

### `src/core/saved-keys.ts`

- Line 1:

  > API KEYS, CHANGED FROM HOME'S ADMIN TAB. 1 October 2026 (migration 067).
  >
  > Lakhbir: Admin's tab is "back end access … update the API keys and save them". Until now a key could only be changed
  > in the key file on the server, or in the test website's settings on Vercel.
  >
  > WHAT IS SHOWN: each key's name, what it is for, and where its value comes from — saved here (when, and by whom), the
  > key file or the website's settings, or not set. NEVER A VALUE, NOT EVEN A PART OF ONE, ONCE SAVED.
  > SAVING: Admin only, with their own password typed again. The value is sealed with AES-256-GCM under CAPREBATE_MFA_KEY
  > (the key that already seals each person's authenticator secret, src/core/mfa-seal.ts), with the key's name bound in so a
  > sealed value copied onto another name does not open. Without a good CAPREBATE_MFA_KEY nothing is saved: a key kept as
  > text in the database is refused, not quietly allowed. CAPREBATE_MFA_KEY itself is not offered (it cannot seal itself),
  > nor a retired key. The audit line names the key, never the value.
  > READING: the newest row for a name wins over the key file or the settings; "Use the key file again" adds a row with no
  > value. Every request checks one number (the newest row) and rebuilds the keys only when it has moved, so a key saved on
  > one copy of the website is read by every copy at its next request.

  > 1 OCT 2026 — PORT 587 SPEAKS PLAIN FIRST. IONOS takes mail on 465, secure from the first byte, and on 587, where the
  > conversation starts in plain text and becomes secure with STARTTLS before anything private is said. Until today the
  > adapter opened every port as 465, so a key file saying 587 met a server that hung up before its greeting ("0 the
  > connection closed"). Now 465 is secure from the start, and any other port says EHLO, STARTTLS, and only then — on the
  > secure connection — EHLO again and the login. A server that will not go secure is refused: the password is never sent
  > in plain text. A test's own connector is used as it is.

### `src/modules/survey/pack-sums.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE SURVEY PACK'S SUMS — how the price paid becomes the spend that qualifies. 1 October 2026.
  >
  > Lakhbir: "build the comprehensive report, as best we can and then we engage with a surveyor … each section allowing
  > the surveyor to edit if needed and the numbers matching what they put in, change or take out" — and, of these sums,
  > "this is one thing that cannot fail".
  >
  > THE METHOD IS SECTION 562 OF THE CAPITAL ALLOWANCES ACT 2001, BY REBUILD COST. The price paid, less the bare land, is
  > the price of the building. The building's rebuild cost today is its floor area times a whole-building rate (BCIS).
  > Each element that may qualify — the electrics, a lift, the clinical basins — has its own rebuild cost (how much times
  > a rate) and the share of it that qualifies. The price of the building is then shared out in the same proportion as
  > the rebuild cost: what qualifies = the building's price × the qualifying rebuild cost ÷ the whole rebuild cost. The
  > main pool and the special rate pool are shared out the same way.
  >
  > THIS FILE ONLY ADDS UP. No database, no clock, no page: given the inputs, the same answer every time, so it can be
  > tested on tens of thousands of made-up packs (test/pack-sums.test.ts). The rules it keeps, each tested:
  >
  >   · EVERY AMOUNT IS WHOLE PENCE, worked in BigInt, so nothing is lost to floating point and nothing overflows. Each
  >     rounding is to the nearest penny, a half penny up — and there are exactly four of them (a line's rebuild cost,
  >     its qualifying part, the whole rebuild cost, and the two shares), each named where it happens.
  >   · THE POOLS ADD UP EXACTLY. The main pool is rounded; the special rate pool is what qualifies less the main pool.
  >     So main + special = what qualifies, to the penny, always.
  >   · NOTHING IS GUESSED (N4). One value missing anywhere — a count, a rate, a percentage, a pool, the price, the land,
  >     the floor area, the building rate — and there is NO total: `qualifying_pence` is null and `needed` names every
  >     gap. A partial total would read as an answer.
  >   · A PROBLEM STOPS THE TOTAL TOO: the land at or above the price; elements that cost more than the whole building;
  >     a whole building that costs nothing. Each is named in words.
  >   · A LINE TAKEN OUT counts for nothing, and a line counted as 0 is the same as taking it out.

### `src/modules/survey/anchor-quarantine.ts`

- Line 1:

  > Caprebate — Anchor Quarantine
  > Board item 12830183464. Phase 3, item 4.
  >
  > Anchoring is real and well evidenced: a surveyor who has seen our estimate
  > before forming their own view drifts toward it. That drift destroys the
  > independence which is the only thing making their signature worth anything.
  >
  > So the client-facing ESTIMATE is withheld from the surveyor until they have
  > committed their own figures. Three parts:
  >
  >   1. the quarantine     — structurally unreadable, not merely hidden in a UI
  >   2. the release        — automatic on commitment; no discretion, no queue-jumping
  >   3. the log            — append-only, hash-chained, timestamped. The evidence
  >                           that the process was followed.
  >
  > The quarantine does a second job nobody asked for but everyone needs: by
  > freezing the surveyor's pre-release figures it MEASURES anchoring, because
  > post-release amendments can be compared against the estimate they were
  > exposed to. That measurement feeds 12830166861 and 12818968809.

### `src/modules/survey/surveyor-crm.ts`

- Line 1:

  > Caprebate — Surveyor CRM: rate library and adoption metric
  > Board item 12818968809. Phase 3, item 6.
  >
  > When a surveyor overrides one of our pre-filled rates, that override is kept
  > and becomes part of that surveyor's own rate library, offered back to them on
  > later jobs. And we track the adoption rate per field — how often our pre-fill
  > survives untouched.
  >
  > THE POINT OF THE ADOPTION RATE. It is the only honest evidence we will ever
  > have about whether our estimates are any good. Nobody grades our pre-fills;
  > a chartered surveyor either leaves them alone or does not, on real jobs, with
  > their own signature at the end of it. That is a revealed preference, and it
  > is worth more than any amount of internal review.
  >
  > WHICH IS WHY IT MUST BE MEASURED HONESTLY. Two disciplines do most of the work:
  >
  >   1. STRATIFY BY WHAT WAS SHOWN. If we pre-fill from the surveyor's OWN
  >      library and they accept it, that is not evidence our estimate is good —
  >      it is evidence they agree with themselves. Only PLATFORM_DEFAULT
  >      pre-fills count toward calibration.
  >
  >   2. DIRECTION BEATS MAGNITUDE. Overrides scattered symmetrically around zero
  >      mean our central estimate is right and our precision is poor. Overrides
  >      that all go one way mean we are biased, which is a different and more
  >      fixable problem. Report both.
  >
  > Feeds the blocked calibration item 12830166861.

## 2 Oct 2026: Phase 5

### `src/integrations/registers/name-exclusion.ts`

- Line 1:

  > Caprebate — Name Exclusion Register & Automated Assertion
  > Board item 12818313893. Phase 5, item 7.
  >
  > The rule, in one sentence: no register ingestion may write a natural
  > person's name to storage except the two documented exceptions (Companies
  > House PSC, and an individual HM Land Registry proprietor). Everything
  > else — assessor names, registered managers, nominated individuals,
  > responsible individuals, directors, secretaries, trustees, applicants,
  > agents, objectors, neighbours, ratepayers, registered persons — is
  > retrieved (where the source API forces it) and never recorded.
  >
  > This module is the single typed source of the source-by-source register
  > documented on the board item. The Monday doc's Part A is generated FROM
  > this data, not written alongside it, so the register and the code cannot
  > drift apart: change the KEEP/EXCLUDE list here and the documentation is
  > wrong until someone updates both, which is the same discipline the
  > source register (caprebate-source-register.ts, board 12830181420)
  > already applies to provenance. The two modules are deliberately
  > independent: that file governs what a source may write about a BUILDING
  > (provenance, licence, grade); this one governs what a source may write
  > about a PERSON (a name, or a field that identifies one). A field could
  > pass one and fail the other, and both must be checked.
  >
  > Fail-closed is the load-bearing property, not a footnote. A source that
  > is not in NAME_EXCLUSION_POLICY cannot write anything at all — not
  > because its fields have been checked and found safe, but because nobody
  > has looked yet. The same rule applies field-by-field on a REGISTERED
  > source: a field that is neither on the KEEP list, the EXCLUDE list, nor
  > one of the two named exceptions is UNCLASSIFIED and is refused, on the
  > ground that an uncatalogued field might be exactly the personal-name
  > field nobody has added to the policy yet. A new source or a new field
  > must earn its way onto a list before it can be written; it is never
  > assumed innocent by default.
  >
  > LIA cross-reference: board doc id 46389172 (item 5). This module is what
  > safeguards S1 and S11 refer to (LIA §7.3 table). The LIA supplies the
  > lawful-basis balancing test; this module supplies, and enforces, the
  > field-level rule the LIA depends on. Do not restate the balancing test
  > here — read it there.
  >
  > Runs on Node >= 22.6 with type stripping (`node file.ts`). No enums, no
  > namespaces, no parameter properties — those are not strippable.

### `src/modules/survey/pack-legal.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE SURVEY PACK'S LEGAL CHECK — can the client claim on these fixtures at all? 2 October 2026.
  >
  > Lakhbir, 1 October 2026, agreeing that the legal check comes before the survey: on a building bought from an owner
  > who could claim, the buyer's claim on the fixtures can be worth nothing unless the value was fixed — a section 198
  > election, or a tribunal application, within two years (CAA 2001 s.187A) — however good the survey is.
  >
  > THE LAW IS THE ENGINE'S, NOT THIS FILE'S. The questions are the sector's own (its "What happened" and "History of …"
  > groups, built by CB_S187A.questions and the election questions), chosen by WHICH FACTS THEY SET, so the five sectors'
  > question sets are read the same way without a list of ids to keep in step. The answers are replayed through each
  > question's own `showIf` and `onSet`, in the sector's order, exactly as the engine's flow does; then the engine's two
  > assessments, CB_ELECTION.assess and CB_S187A.assess, give the position. This file only turns that into a verdict:
  >
  >   GREEN    the rules do not reach this claim, or they are met (OFF, SATISFIED; no election, or a complete one).
  >   URGENT   there is still time to fix the value — the claim can go ahead, and the deadline is shown (LIVE).
  >   AMBER    not known yet: a question unanswered, or a position the engine cannot settle (INDET). Blocks approval.
  >   RED      the claim on these fixtures fails (NIL, or a nominal election over the fixtures generally). Blocks it.
  >
  > "NOT KNOWN" IS NEVER A PASS (the engine's own rule, kept): an unanswered question is AMBER, and "not sure" is an
  > answer the engine treats as unknown. Where an election or a disposal value statement caps the claim, the cap is
  > returned, and the pack may not be approved above it (stage 3).

### `src/modules/survey/photo-upload.ts`

- Line 1:

  > FULL-SIZE PHOTOS, SENT STRAIGHT TO THE FILE STORE, LOCKED ON THE PHONE. 2 October 2026.
  >
  > Lakhbir asked whether the test website's 4.5 MB a send could be raised. It cannot: it is Vercel's fixed limit on a
  > request to the website. So each photo goes from the phone STRAIGHT TO THE PRIVATE FILE STORE (Vercel Blob), never
  > through the website: "go with option 2"; "Lock on the phone"; "100 photos, 25 MB each"; the mock-up, "Yes, build it
  > as shown".
  >
  > HOW. The page's one script (src/modules/survey/photo-upload-script.ts) asks to START a send (`startUpload`): the server makes a
  > ONE-TIME LOCK for it — an RSA-2048 key pair — and gives the phone its public half; the private half is kept in the
  > database, itself encrypted with the store's key. For each photo the phone makes a fresh AES-256-GCM key, locks the
  > photo with it, and locks that key with the public half (RSA-OAEP, SHA-256). It asks for a SLOT (`slotFor`): one
  > address in the store for exactly that file, for half an hour, at most the size it said (on the test website a Blob
  > presigned PUT; on any other copy, our own route, `putLocal`). It sends the locked photo there, then says it is DONE
  > (`finishSlot`): the server reads it, opens it with the private half, and treats the photo exactly as a photo sent
  > through the page — JPEG or PNG by its first bytes, at most 25 MB, hidden details taken out, ENCRYPTED with the
  > store's key and kept as not yet sorted (survey-evidence.ts `keep`) — then removes the locked upload. Vercel never
  > holds a photo it can read.
  >
  > WHO. A client of the job's company, for their own send only; with "nobody is in any of these photos" ticked. An
  > upload never finished is removed by the SWEEP (`sweepUploads`) after a day: at the next send, and whenever the outside
  > timer wakes the website (/hooks/read-replies). Each slot's outcome — KEPT, REFUSED or ABANDONED — is recorded once
  > (migration 076). Admin or Sales sort the photos as before (survey-evidence.ts `sortPhotos`).

### `src/modules/survey/survey-video.ts`

- Line 1:

  > A VIDEO OF THE BUILDING, SENT FROM THE PHONE IN LOCKED PIECES. 2 October 2026.
  >
  > Lakhbir: "we need to add an option of upload video"; the limits, "10 minutes, 1 GB each"; how videos are kept,
  > "Same as photos" — locked on the phone, the place it was filmed taken out, encrypted, kept for testing 7 years, seen by
  > the client, the assigned surveyor, Admin, Sales and the data protection officer.
  >
  > HOW. A video is far bigger than one request to the test website may carry (4.5 MB), and than a phone can lock in one
  > go. So the page's script (src/modules/survey/photo-upload-script.ts) cuts it into pieces of 4 MB. The send gets a one-time lock
  > (`startVideo`, as a photo send does); each piece is locked on the phone with a fresh key, given its own place
  > (`videoSlot`: a Blob presigned PUT on the test website, or our own route — `putVideoLocal` — on any other copy or
  > when the store gives no address), sent, and reported (`finishPiece`): the server opens it, checks its size, and keeps
  > it ENCRYPTED with the store's key at survey-videos/<video>/<n>; the locked piece is removed. When every piece has come
  > (`finishVideo`) the video is checked — an MP4 or QuickTime file (its `ftyp`), at most ten minutes (its `mvhd`) — and
  > every place written in its header (ISO 6709 co-ordinates, as phones write them: `©xyz`, or the Apple location key)
  > is blanked IN PLACE, the same length, so nothing else in the file moves. Then it is kept. A refused or abandoned video's
  > pieces are removed.
  >
  > PLAYBACK in pieces (`videoBytes`): a browser asks for a range of bytes, and is answered at most one piece at a time —
  > which is what an iPhone needs to play and seek, and keeps every answer under the test website's limit.

- Line 417:

  > Below this an adoption rate is not a rate, it is an anecdote.
  >
  > RE-DERIVED against the AD-HOC engagement model (item 12927112944, Phase 10
  > finding: MIN_N_FOR_RATE and selfConsistency() were both set assuming repeat
  > engagements with the same surveyor). Raised from 5 to 7. This constant gates
  > the POOLED, cross-surveyor adoption()/divergences() cohort signal, which was
  > never itself repeat-engagement-dependent — `adoption()` already pools across
  > ALL_SURVEYORS by default. What ad-hoc engagement changes is the composition
  > of that pool: instead of a handful of repeat observations from one surveyor
  > whose personal calibration is already known, each observation now comes from
  > a different, unfamiliar surveyor. That adds a between-surveyor variance
  > component (differing house style, risk appetite, familiarity with a platform
  > seen for the first time) on top of the estimate error the metric exists to
  > measure, so more observations are needed before the pooled median is a
  > trustworthy signal rather than noise from whichever surveyors happened to be
  > in the sample. Still provisional — a reasoned adjustment for a changed
  > assumption, not a value fitted to real ad-hoc data, because none exists yet.

  >    ============================================================================
  >    THE DEFECT. Specification section 4.2 builds both replacement-cost components
  >    as
  >
  >        A = sum(qty x rate x (1 + prelims) x (1 + fees) x index)
  >        B = nonqual_rate_per_m2 x area x (1 + prelims) x (1 + fees) x index
  >
  >    with prelims defaulting to 0.18. VOA guidance on estimated replacement cost
  >    is that on-costs - site set-up, scaffolding, plant hire, site management,
  >    insurances - are ALREADY INSIDE the estimated replacement cost. Multiplying
  >    by a further 1.18 counts them twice, and it inflates A and B together.
  >
  >    WHY THE SIZE OF THE ERROR IS NOT 18%. The residual model divides:
  >    m = PC / (A + B + C). A common uplift on A and B partly cancels in the ratio
  >    m x A. It does not cancel completely, because C - bare-site land value - is
  >    not uplifted. So the double count shifts value from land into buildings and
  >    plant, and the qualifying figure moves by materially less than 18%. It still
  >    moves, always in the direction of OVERSTATING the claim, and it moves most on
  >    the properties with the highest land fraction. Overstatement is the direction
  >    that loses an enquiry.
  >
  >    ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  >    IS THIS ACTUALLY LICENCE-GATED? A QUESTION FOR LAKHBIR, NOT A DECISION.
  >
  >    The board marked this blocked on VOA licence clearance (that licence was
  >    dropped on 4 Oct 2026; Phase 157a corrected this text). Reading the change
  >    itself: turning this gate on sets a multiplier to 1.0 and deletes a
  >    parameter. It reproduces no VOA table, quotes no VOA figure, and needs no
  >    VOA data to compute. The only VOA-derived thing involved is the KNOWLEDGE
  >    that on-costs sit inside ERC - and that knowledge is what tells us our own
  >    arithmetic counts them twice.
  >
  >    Knowing a double count exists is not the same as republishing the data that
  >    revealed it. On that reading this looks over-blocked, and it is the one fix
  >    of the four that could ship on its own.
  >
  >    Two arguments the other way, which is why this is a question and not a
  >    conclusion. First, if the licence terms restrict DERIVED WORKS rather than
  >    reproduction, a model shaped by VOA methodology may be caught even where no
  >    VOA number appears in it. Second, E2 and E3 touch the same expression: ship
  >    E2 alone and A and B carry a corrected prelims term beside an uncorrected
  >    flat 15% fee term, which is a defensible interim but is a state someone has
  >    to be told about rather than discover.
  >
  >    NOT UNBLOCKED HERE. The gate is false like the others. Flagged for decision.
  >    ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  >
  >    DO NOT "TIDY" THIS INTO THE FIT-OUT PATH. There is a trap here and it has
  >    caught people before. JD Wetherspoon plc v HMRC [2012] UKUT 42 holds that
  >    preliminaries and professional fees DO apportion to qualifying plant and
  >    machinery, pro rata, on an invoice-based claim - and that they are routinely
  >    missed, which understates claims. Module-00-Master-Engine-Specification.md
  >    line 104 says exactly that.
  >
  >    Wetherspoon and LEG-E2 are not in conflict. They are about different paths:
  >
  >      INVOICE / FIT-OUT path     real prelims and fees appear as their own lines
  >                                 in a cost package. Wetherspoon says apportion
  >                                 them to qualifying P&M rather than dropping
  >                                 them. ADD.
  >      RESIDUAL / VALUATION path  the price-book rate already contains on-costs.
  >                                 Adding a further uplift double counts.
  >                                 DO NOT ADD.
  >
  >    Same words, opposite treatment, because one is a real invoiced cost being
  >    allocated and the other is a modelled cost already inclusive. LEG-E2 changes
  >    the residual path ONLY. Anyone applying it to the invoice path would
  >    understate every fit-out claim and would be reversing Wetherspoon. Hence
  >    costBasis below, which must be stated and is never defaulted.
  >
  >    ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  >    PHASE 132, 14 SEPTEMBER 2026 - ON-COSTS ARE A FACT ABOUT THE BOOK.
  >    "There is no parameter anywhere for whether the unit rate is on-cost-
  >    inclusive" (4 September). The residual-path argument above holds for a
  >    replacement-cost rate that already includes on-costs. It does NOT hold for
  >    an element rate that excludes them - there, adding preliminaries once is
  >    right and dropping them understates. leg_e2_drop_prelims_from_erc cannot
  >    tell the two apart; it drops prelims on every residual job. So a second,
  >    alternative gate, leg_e2_oncosts_by_price_source, reads the answer off the
  >    job's named price book (CB_PRICE_SOURCES[price_source].rates_include_oncosts):
  >      true    factor 1, flag LEG_E2_ONCOSTS_IN_RATES
  >      false   1 + preliminaries, today's figure, flag LEG_E2_ONCOSTS_EXCLUDED_BY_SOURCE
  >      null, "unsure" or absent   E_ONCOSTS_BASIS_UNKNOWN - never defaulted either way
  >    An unnamed or unlisted book refuses with E_PRICE_SOURCE_REQUIRED. Both
  >    leg_e2 gates on refuses with E_GATE_CONFLICT, the same interlock shape as the
  >    fee gates. The invoice path is untouched by either gate.
  >    ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  >    ============================================================================

  > after a 413 on a kept-alive connection the next request on it hung about 6 s and was reset: reading stopped part-way,
  > the rest of the body was left in the connection, and the connection was kept. Now the rest of a body over its cap is
  > read and dropped - up to DRAIN_MAX more, so the sender is never cut off mid-send and sees the answer - and the 413
  > says "Connection: close", so the connection ends when the answer has gone and nothing left in it is taken for the
  > next request. A body more than DRAIN_MAX over its cap is refused at once and the connection closed under it.
  > server.ts tells this file which response each request is answered on.

  > recommendation for him to check: twelve months after it was closed. A deletion cannot be undone, so — like the
  > message clean-up before it was answered — the job ships OFF and deletes nothing until the officer approves the period
  > and that approval is recorded; then a scheduled run of `node src/core/cli.ts sweep-enquiries` applies it.
  >
  > TWO KINDS OF ENQUIRY, NAMED:
  >   1. THE CONTACT FORM (/enquiry, `website_enquiries`, migration 031). One closed by staff (status CLOSED, its
  >      `handled_at` the day it was closed) is due twelve months after that day. This job writes the deletion log entry
  >      FIRST, then deletes the row, in one transaction — one entry per enquiry, naming its kind and id, never a word of
  >      it and never the person. An enquiry that became a lead (status LEAD) is a lead now, and is not this job's.
  >  *   2. THE FOUR-STAGE FUNNEL (`leads` with an `enquiry_id`, migration 061). A funnel enquiry is a CRM lead, tied to its
  >      organisation, its contacts and any booking. PHASE 157 (the sweep, 6 October 2026) BUILT ITS DELETION PATH, under
  >      the same switch and the same period: a lead LOST more than the period ago (its `updated_at`, the day it was
  >      marked lost) is deleted with the funnel's own rows that hang off it — `leadDeletionPlan` says exactly which.
  >        WHAT GOES: the lead; its contacts and what they answered about consent; its bookings, their changes and video
  >        meetings; the emails written to it; its staff tasks, automation runs and enquiry checks. And, ONLY when every
  >        lead of its organisation is a lost funnel enquiry past the period, the organisation too: its properties,
  >        assessment and answers, sealed estimate, research rows and the draft that made it.
  >        WHAT STAYS: anything with a reason of its own — a claim, an engagement or signature, an invoice, a complaint,
  >        a rights request, a breach entry, a document, a client message, an identity or due-diligence check, an
  >        introducer's record, a call log — and if any such row hangs off the lead or its organisation, NOTHING is
  >        deleted and the job says which table held it. The audit log keeps its rows (ids only, never a word). One
  >        deletion log entry per lead (FUNNEL_LEAD) and per organisation (FUNNEL_BUSINESS), written FIRST, in the same
  >        transaction: migration 093's triggers admit a delete only for rows those entries name.
  > A LIVE LEGAL HOLD STOPS IT (record kind WEBSITE_ENQUIRY, by its id; LEAD and COMPANY for a funnel enquiry). N4: an

### `src/modules/survey/pack-grants.ts`

- Line 1:

  > THE SURVEY PACK'S GRANTS — chapter 15. Phase 153a, 4 October 2026: F-15's remainder.
  >
  > Rulebook F (01-rulebooks/Caprebate-Statutory-Rules-Register-F-Contributions-And-Grants-v1.md): money from someone
  > else reduces the spend "to the extent that" it met it (s.532, F-R1), and F3 says "trace it to cost elements; do not
  > pro-rate yet". Until this file, a grant on the claim record (claim_grants, migration 015) was matched only in words,
  > and nothing took it off anything: the survey pack's sums (src/modules/survey/pack-sums.ts) had no grant in them at all.
  >
  > TWO ROUTES, AND THE SWITCH CB_CTA.grant_traced_to_elements CHOOSES BETWEEN THEM. It ships OFF.
  >
  >   EQUAL SHARE   the grant_fraction route the public estimate has always used: the grant is a share of the price
  >                 paid, and every item loses that share. A £100,000 grant on a £500,000 price takes 20% off what
  >                 qualifies. OFF, EVERY GRANT TAKES THIS ROUTE.
  >   ITEMS         ON, a grant matched to named rows of the fixture list (claim_grant_elements, migration 078) comes off
  >                 only those rows: it met their spend, so their qualifying part comes down by the share of their spend
  >                 it met, and no other row moves. Split across several rows by their rebuild cost. A grant whose rows
  >                 are none of the pack's counted lines — it paid only for items that never qualify, such as the walls
  >                 or the flats — takes nothing off (Word question 79). A grant matched only in words, or not matched
  >                 at all, keeps the equal share.
  >
  > WHO PAID (F4, F5). Only insurance money after damage is known not to reduce the spend (F-R7). A connected payer — a
  > landlord linked to the client, a company in its group — reduces it unless CB_CTA.connected_contributor_no_reduction is
  > on (F-R10, F-Q1), the same switch the public estimate reads. Everyone else, and a payer not known, reduces it: whether
  > a private payer could claim relief itself (F-R9) is not a fact we hold, and N4 never lets an unknown relieve.
  >
  > N4, IN THIS FILE.
  >   · A grant matched only in words, or not at all, is UNTRACED — never taken as having paid for nothing.
  >   · A grant that reduces and whose amount is not known gives NO TOTAL, and is named in `needed`. A total without it
  >     would read as an answer.
  >   · A pack with no total before grants has none after them.
  >
  > THE ORDER. Grants matched to items come off first, line by line; the equal-share grants then take their share of what
  > is left. Every amount is whole pence in BigInt, each rounding the nearest penny, a half up (pack-sums.ts's own rule).
  > Main pool + special rate pool = what qualifies, to the penny, after grants as before them.
  >
  > PHASE 159i (item 1, Rulebook F F-R12): A THIRD ROUTE, FULL, replaces the equal share where `untraced_full` is on (on
  > in test): a grant that cannot be traced to the items it paid for comes off what qualifies in full — the conservative
  > deduction — after the traced ones. A grant paid to an EARLIER owner (PAST_OWNER) takes nothing off the buyer's sums;
  > it lowers the cap from the earlier sale (s.185, pack-legal.ts). And C23: every route's rows add up to its total.
  >
  > NOTHING HERE READS A DATABASE, A CLOCK OR A SWITCH: the switches are arguments, so both ways are tested
  > (test/pack-grants.test.ts) while the one that ships is off. Whether a grant reduces qualifying spend item by item is
  > the tax adviser's to confirm — FOR THE ACCOUNTANT, ACC-A16.

### `src/integrations/connectors/whatsapp-export.ts`

- Line 1:

  > PHASE 156c, 5 October 2026 — READING A CHAT EXPORTED FROM THE WHATSAPP PHONE. No network, no Meta.
  >
  > Lakhbir chose a manual upload (5 Oct 2026: "go with manual upload, keep photos"): staff talk to clients on the
  > WhatsApp phone, and to keep a conversation they export that one chat (Export chat > Attach media) and upload the
  > .zip on the client's WhatsApp page. This file turns the export's text into messages; src/web/whatsapp-import.ts
  > checks them with a person and saves them.
  >
  > THE TWO LAYOUTS (read from a real iPhone export's 5 October lines only, every word masked, used with consent; and
  > WhatsApp's documented Android form):
  >   iPhone   [05/10/2026, 13:36:43] Name: text           (24-hour; or 1:36:43 PM, with a narrow space before PM)
  >   Android  05/10/2026, 13:36 - Name: text              (no seconds)
  > Lines without a date belong to the message above. Messages are separated by CRLF on the iPhone, while a message's
  > own line breaks are a bare LF; both are read the same way here. A U+200E (left-to-right mark) may stand before the
  > line, before an attachment and before WhatsApp's own words; it is never part of what a person wrote.
  >
  > WHAT IS RECOGNISED: an attachment ("<attached: FILE>" on the iPhone, "FILE (file attached)" on Android, with any
  > words before it kept as its caption); a file left out of the export ("<Media omitted>", "image omitted"); a deleted
  > message ("This message was deleted." / "You deleted this message."), kept as WhatsApp wrote it; an edit
  > ("<This message was edited>"), marked; WhatsApp's own notices (end-to-end encryption, joined, changed number…),
  > skipped. An empty message is skipped.
  >
  > DATES are read day first (UK). If no day number in the file is above 12, month first would also make sense, and
  > the check step says so. TIMES are UK local time (Europe/London), turned into an exact moment across the clock
  > change; the export carries no time zone.

  > Lakhbir chose this over a live connection to Meta (5 Oct 2026: "go with manual upload, keep photos"). Staff talk to

  >

  >   2. CHECK (`importCheck`). How many messages and files, the first and last date, who is us and who is the client,
  >      and from which date to keep them — an export always holds the WHOLE history of the chat. Warnings: dates that
  >      could be read month first; a contact who did not tick the WhatsApp box (their messages are kept: Lakhbir,
  >      5 Oct 2026, "kept in").
  >   3. SAVE (`saveImport`). Each message from that date into whatsapp_messages (IN or OUT, the message's own time),
  >      tied to this upload in whatsapp_import_lines. A newer copy of the same chat adds only what is not there yet.
  >      Files: from the kept .zip at once; otherwise the script sends each needed one (`addImportFile`), each sealed
  >      in the file store as a fetched WhatsApp attachment is.
  >
  > Nothing here contacts Meta or anyone else. The copies follow the same keep-and-delete rules as other client
  > messages (Lakhbir, 5 Oct 2026, "yes same rules").

  > itself, and HOMEDATA_TERMS (the source register) keeps every report channel closed until Homedata's terms for title

  > ONE VERSION AFTER SIGN-OFF. PHASE 159a, 9 October 2026, from the stress test of that day (C3, C5, and L3 in the
  > Lockwood Surgery run).
  >
  > What went wrong: a surveyor could approve a new version of the survey pack, and answer the legal check again, after
  > the tax adviser had signed off and the claim had moved on to Reports, or after the claim had stopped. The client's
  > report, their acceptance and the defence pack stayed on the signed version, while the amendment-window gate read the
  > newer version's purchase date. So the claim closed on a report whose purchase date was not the one the gate checked.
  >
  > THE RULE NOW:
  >   · LOCKED. Once a claim is past the tax adviser's sign-off (Reports, Invoice, Defence pack, Closed), or has stopped
  >     at an exit, its valuation is fixed: no pack approval and no legal-check answer is taken (src/web/pack-approve.ts,
  >     src/web/pack-legal.ts). A claim on hold is judged by the stage it returns to.
  >   · REOPENED, ON PURPOSE. The only way to change the figures then is "Reopen the valuation": an admin moves the claim
  >     back to Valuation, with a reason (the claim's own REOPEN move, src/modules/crm/pipeline.ts). A reopen to any stage up to
  >     and including the tax adviser's sign-off SETS ASIDE what was released on the old figures, and the claim page says
  >     each one: the tax adviser's sign-off, the client report and the accountant's pack as issued (marked superseded),
  >     the client's acceptance of that report, and any defence pack. Nothing is deleted: every record stays, and the
  >     readers below look only at what came after the reopen.
  >
  > `voidLine` is the moment of the latest such reopen. A sign-off, an acceptance or an issued deliverable from before it
  > no longer counts.

  >   client on every trigger and never asks about the deal at all. The fact
  >   moves real money: it narrows the qualifying range and it decides whether
  >   the s.187A machinery runs. Supplying it on facts the engine's own flow

  >   the accounting period end that CB_CASH turns into a statutory amendment
  >   window. A partial date silently parsed is a wrong window in front of a
  >   client, and the funnel never asks for the accounting period end anyway, so
  >   the window cannot be derived from what the six screens hold.
  >
  > Q3 works -> `base_amount`   (PHASE 159c: the works ARE now mapped, as `events`
  >   above, each event on its own cost; what follows is why they are never added
  >   to the one amount.) IT WOULD DOUBLE-COUNT, AND CB_FRONTDOOR HAS A
  >   FUNCTION WHOSE ONLY JOB IS TO PREVENT THAT. `worksHeadingFor` re-words the
  >   works question for a refurbishment or a fit-out because "asking 'any work
  >   done?' against that property invites the client to enter the same money a
  >   second time, and the figure inflates by exactly the amount they were most

  >   demolition   taking out old plant (s.26) — it follows the new plant
  >   other        building work that does not qualify        repairs   the part that is a repair (a revenue deduction)
  >   prelims      preliminaries                               fees      professional fees
  >
  > THE SUM: what qualifies directly is the plant (main + special) with the builder's work and the demolition that follow
  > it; the preliminaries and the fees are shared out over every direct cost in the same proportion, so the share on the
  > plant qualifies and the share on the repairs goes with the repairs. The pools split what qualifies as the plant does:
  > main rounded, special the rest, so the two add up to the penny. With no plant in it, nothing qualifies.
  >
  > N4 AND THE CHECK. Every value must be given (0 is a value); one missing and there is no total. The parts must add up to
  > the final account exactly, or there is no total and the difference is named.

  >
  > The stress test of 9 October 2026 (C13, C15, C17, C18; the Lockwood run, L4): the return entries showed writing-down
  > allowances only, every spend in one period, the special rate pool at 6% in every year, no small-pools write-off and no
  > structures allowance. A recent refit can take 100% in year one. Lakhbir's target, 9 October 2026: "the highest figure
  > we can defend". So each PART of a claim — the purchase, and each piece of work since (Phase 159c) — is worked out on
  > its own, from the approved version alone:
  >
  >   ITS PERIOD (items 4, 7, 8). The route Phase 159d gave it, frozen with the version: W1 goes into the period its own
  >   date falls in; W2 into the first period whose return is still open; W3 is not claimed. Those are the periods the
  >   amendment window read, from the client's checked year end — one period source, so the window and the spreadsheet
  >   cannot disagree (C15).
  >
  >   ITS FIRST-YEAR RELIEF (item 1), ON W1 ONLY — W2 is writing-down allowances only, and an unknown route grants nothing
  >   (N4). The annual investment allowance (s.38A, £1,000,000 a period, shared across a group or related businesses)
  >   where this period's headroom is RECORDED — not for a partnership with a company partner (s.38A(3)), and not where
  >   that is not known; it goes on the special rate pool first (Rulebook I section 2, CA23084). Then, on NEW AND UNUSED
  >   plant only: a company's full expensing on the main pool and 50% first-year allowance on the special rate pool, spent
  >   from 1 April 2023 (CA23174AA); the 40% allowance on the main pool spent from 1 January 2026 (s.45U) for anyone who
  >   does not have full expensing. Work the client paid for is new plant (OUR READING); a purchase is second-hand, unless
  >   the building was bought new and never used from its developer (OUR READING; BOUGHT_NEW_FROM_DEVELOPER). The
  >   super-deduction (2021 to 2023) needs a contract signed after 3 March 2021, which nothing records, so it is named and
  >   not taken. A RE-DERIVED PREMISE (standing instruction step 8): the phase prompt said a second-hand purchase takes
  >   writing-down allowances only. The annual investment allowance is not limited to new plant (Rulebook I section 2:
  >   "virtually all plant and machinery qualifying expenditure"), so a W1 purchase takes it where headroom is recorded;
  >   only full expensing and the first-year allowances are barred to it. Put to the tax adviser (Word question 257).
  >
  >   THE STRUCTURES AND BUILDINGS ALLOWANCE (item 2). Work: the part of the work that is neither plant nor repair (the
  >   final account less the plant and the repair part), on work dated wholly from November 2018 — its date standing for
  >   its contract date, which must be from 29 October 2018 (OUR READING) — from the month after the work, at the engine's
  >   dated rate (2% before April 2020, 3% after). A purchase from 29 October 2018: from the seller's allowance statement
  >   (s.270IA; SBA_STATEMENT_HELD and SBA_QUALIFYING_EXPENDITURE), from the purchase date. None on a dwelling — supported
  >   living homes (s.270CF); care homes, surgeries and hospitals are not residential use (s.270CF(3)). W2: from the
  >   first open period; the years before are lost, not carried. Word question 259.
  >
  >   THE POOLS (item 3). The writing-down rates are the engine's dated table (CB_RATES: 8% special rate before April
  >   2019, 20% main before April 2012, 14% from April 2026, blended across a change), and a pool of £1,000 or less is
  >   written off in full (s.56A). Worked in whole pence: every row adds up.
  >
  > NOTHING HERE STATES A RATE. Every rate and date comes from the engine (Rulebook I rule 7.1).
